mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined over the prior month, or Rank IC over 3 years remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeded 4.5% for two months, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicate sharp consumer demand contraction, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 0.5% and RSAFS declines > 0.5% in past month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS declined >0.5%, or Rank IC over 3 years remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months), increased borrowing costs reduce corporate investment and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month signals robust manufacturing activity that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO increased >0.5% in past month, or Rank IC over 3 years remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When core inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5% YoY for two months, it signals persistent inflation prompting aggressive central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeded 3.5% YoY for two months, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market weakening that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth <0.2% and UNRATE >4.0%, or Rank IC over 3 years remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 1400 thousand units and RSAFS growth > 1.5% YoY), peak economic activity triggers profit-taking and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.02.
